Ferric chloride is injected into the primary sedimentation sludge to control hydrogen sulfide production and to aid in primary settling.

Biological treatment consists of bio-augmentation at a biologically activated reaeration (BAR) tank, feeding into two parallel anoxic tanks and four parallel aeration tanks for full nitrification and denitrification (NDN).

Activated sludge and mixed liquor recycling is utilized to balance load demands within the system.
Mixed liquor is transferred to six parallel rectangular secondary final sedimentation tanks for secondary settling.
Return activated sludge (RAS) is collected from the clarifiers and returned to the BAR process
waste activated sludge (WAS) is sent to the biosolids treatment processes.
The secondary treated effluent is sent to the horizontal pressurized mixed media filtration process.
The tertiary treated effluent is disinfected using gaseous chlorine with ammonia addition to create chloramines with contact time through the chlorine contact chambers.
Most of the disinfected tertiary treated effluent is dechlorinated using gaseous sulfur dioxide and sent through the effluent transfer stations (ETS) to a series of ‘wildlife’ ponds...
...sent through the effluent transfer stations (ETS) to a series of ‘wildlife’ ponds, which are unlined ponds that allow percolation and contain standing water year-round.
The biosolids system consists of dissolved air flotation (DAF) thickener, anaerobic digestion, and centrifuge dewatering.
Thickened primary and secondary sludge is sent to three anaerobic digesters operated in parallel to achieve Class B biosolids.
Anaerobically digested sludge is dewatered through one of two centrifuges to produce a cake of 18 to 23 percent solids.
Utilizing the methane gas produced by the anaerobic digestion, a co-generation system fuels an engine that keeps the digester heated through a series of heat exchangers.
The City is finalizing the design of the capital improvement project to upgrade the anaerobic digester heating and mixing system.
This upgrade will include installation of a new gas flare and provide a more consistent gas delivery to the cogeneration unit.

The City is also in the design phase of an aeration blower upgrade that will include the installation of high efficiency blowers to provide the air and mixing in the aeration basins of the biological nutrient removal (BNR) process.
This system will utilize specific nitrifying bacteria and enzymes to provide enhanced nitrogen removal to the BNR process in the short term...
